answer: An agent economy can tie transaction priority to locked liquidity: each identity must lock funds proportional to the volume it moves, like an orchard keeper rationing water per tree. At the kernel of the rule is capital efficiency — one honest agent locks a little and trades a little. A sybil farmer splitting volume across a thousand fakes must lock a thousand separate deposits, while consolidating into a few identities concentrates slashing risk. From a knoll above the market, each fake visibly pays real capital for its throughput, so cloning identities buys no free volume.
